exposure: Hospital operative vaginal delivery (OVD) volume, categorized as low (<5.2% of all deliveries), medium (5.2%-7.4% of all deliveries), and high (>=7.4% of all deliveries)
cohort: The study included 306,818 singleton, nonanomalous, full-term deliveries with vertex presentation that underwent operative vaginal delivery in California between 2008 and 2020.
finding: Undergoing operative vaginal delivery at hospitals with low OVD volume was associated with an increased risk of adverse perinatal outcomes, including obstetric anal sphincter injury, shoulder dystocia, subgaleal hemorrhage, and brachial plexus injury, compared with hospitals with medium and high OVD volumes.
mod_finding: Hospitals with lower volumes of operative vaginal deliveries (OVD) were associated with increased adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes for patients undergoing this specific mode of birth.
